title: Tooling: make the complete R2 audit 5.37x faster with mutation-path copies
body:
After PR3218's comparator improvement, the retained R2 audit spends most of its time deep-copying entire fixtures for mutations that change one narrow part. This opt-in adapter isolates those write paths while executing every original mutation, nonvacuity check, predicate and exact rejection-message check.

**Complete-audit median: 32.643 → 6.084 seconds, a 5.37x speedup.** Against jackmgaller/#1939's existing checked-marshal copier on the identical workload, the improvement is **10.289 → 6.084 seconds, or 1.69x**.

| Copy mode | Copy interval | Complete audit | Peak RSS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Original deepcopy | 25.603 s | 32.643 s | 138.57 MiB |
| Credited checked marshal | 2.908 s | 10.289 s | 142.12 MiB |
| Mutation paths | 0.061 s | 6.084 s | 135.16 MiB |

BENCHMARK.json records nine fresh serial CPython 3.12.14 processes in alternating order, exact sources, raw timings and memory. All modes use the same complete fixture, comparator, source bindings and added original-fixture guards. Every run retains all **32 semantic mutants** and the same **253 operator decisions (244 accepted, 9 rejected)**. These are one-host measurements; native artifact generation is excluded. The copy-interval improvement is not a whole-audit speedup.

The adapter copies the ancestors of the selected event, gate or recipe and its writable subtree. Untouched cells remain shared and read-only. PROOF.md gives the tree-copy argument and all sixteen literal write footprints. Path copying is established programming practice; no method-priority claim is made. This is source-specific integration, not a general deepcopy replacement for aliased object graphs.

Validation:

- Every one of the 32 actual optimized mutant payloads is compared in full against the original mutation applied to complete deepcopy. Original named rejection checks still execute.
- Complete original fixtures are compared by exact serialized bytes before/after their tests. This guard compares bytes directly, and no predicate-result cache is introduced.
- 100 generated equivalence cases plus controls reject nested-write leakage, out-of-footprint writes, incorrect complete payloads, unknown mutations and altered source hooks.
- Registered Python 3.12 commands, three source-corruption controls, optimized Git-free exports, and Python 3.14 optimized full differential verification pass.
- Metadata/pins, whitespace, all 27 retained-file origin comparisons and all 56 package/input publication-byte comparisons pass. Hosted CI is separate.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/r2-mutation-path-copy
```

Expected: `PASS_R2_PATH_COPY`, `PASS_R2_PATH_COPY_EXPORT`, and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`. Normal fast use is `python3 -I -B research/r2-mutation-path-copy/replay.py`; the registered command deliberately pays for full differential copying.

Only `research/r2-mutation-path-copy/` is added. Base: `463113d675af7410ac91d53a4fed51ec6494eb9a`. Pending PR3218 is retained verbatim at `a93c4f0bfcac21bf9c62c79728c8936e35ebbc3b`, including PR3202 at `259043321323717b7e816d6be38ad5e1f0b69b4c`. All 40 retained/live inputs are authenticated before execution; no pending Git objects are needed for direct replay. Published head: `9f32d16ea188cfba57f6c0d570377be9becb857f`.

This is verification tooling, with no new kappa, supplier admission or recursive multiplication implementation. Selected/frozen sources and default commands are unchanged. PR3208 cleanup, PR3209 reader-cache/host-replication work and PR3219 Fano tables are complementary. Final overlap coverage and concrete next questions are in TASK/README: source/frame/event reconstruction now dominates this caller, while another caller needs its own proven mutation footprint.

Credit 24kHandsome1201/#3202, Tekalign/#3218, jackmgaller/#1939, Sagar Thakrar/#1781, ywz65/#2638, Charles Bethin/#662 and the full native/construction lineage preserved in NOTICE.md and retained notices. New work by Tekalign (@tekuuu), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in profiling, implementation, proof, testing, measurements and writing. Apache-2.0; no independent human or proof-kernel review claimed.
